findings.quote: and they pick those that have these on one side only, not running off in every direction
findings.problem: Greek has a lacuna here: καὶ ταύτας *** ἔχοντες λαμβάνονται * ** οὐκ ἐναλλάξ. The English fills the gap with 'on one side only' and reads on as if the text were whole; the transmitted words are only 'having these ... they are taken ... not alternately (οὐκ ἐναλλάξ)'.
findings.proposed_fix: and having these [...] they are taken [...] not alternately [text lost in the Greek]

units.note: Rest of chapter checked and accurate; the lacuna is the only issue.
Lacuna at *** is already marked [...] in the English; numbers (50 and 30 stades, 300 each) agree.

findings.problem: τὴν δ᾽ ἐφεδρείαν ἀπέστειλε, συντάξας ἐπὶ τοὺς ἄκρους ἐπιβαλεῖν: the ἐφεδρεία is the covering/outpost force sent ahead to occupy the hill summits (called 'outpost' in chapters 21-22), not a rearguard.

units.note: καθ᾽ ὅσον ... κατὰ τοσοῦτον correctly rendered.
ἐξ ἀσπίδος = by the left, correct.

findings.quote: one part was locked in close combat with those fighting
findings.problem: Greek has a lacuna: τὰ μὲν συνεχῆ τοῖς διαγωνιζομένοις ***, so the predicate is missing (only 'the part contiguous to those fighting ...'). The English supplies a verb and reads on as whole.
findings.proposed_fix: one part, adjoining those fighting, [...] [text lost in the Greek]
